summary: Offline bundle hash mismatch after air-gap transfer (artifact modified during unzip/text conversion)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports Redwood Private offline install failing in preflight with "hash mismatch" after transferring the offline bundle via removable media into an air-gapped environment.
- Signature verification appears to pass on the original bundle in the connected staging area, but fails after extraction inside the air-gapped network.

Impact
- Blocks upgrade/install for Ion Fabrication’s factory-floor cluster (air-gapped). Customer stuck on prior bundle version and cannot proceed with scheduled maintenance window.

Customer context
- Ion Fabrication (Private / air-gapped). Bundle delivered via secured USB + internal scanning gateway.
- Customer operators are extracting bundle on Windows jump host, then copying extracted directory to a RHEL host where the installer runs.

Environment
- Installer: redwood-private-installer v1.18.3 (per customer)
- Bundle: Redwood Private 2026.01.0 offline bundle (build ID referenced in manifest)
- OS: Windows Server 2019 jump host + RHEL 8.8 install host

Steps to reproduce (as reported)
1) Download bundle to connected staging machine.
2) Copy bundle to USB.
3) On Windows jump host, extract the archive.
4) Copy extracted folder to RHEL host.
5) Run: redwood-private-installer install --air-gapped --bundle-path /mnt/offline/redwood-private-bundle

Observed behavior
- Preflight fails closed with hash mismatch errors.

Key error output (customer paste)
- "Preflight: bundle integrity check failed"
- "E_BUNDLE_HASH_MISMATCH: sha256 mismatch for artifacts/manifests/redwood-private.yaml"
- "expected: 7b1f7f9c4b8a0a0f… (from manifest)"
- "actual:   1d2d2f2c68e1d65e… (computed from disk)"

Notes
- Customer initially suspected USB corruption; they re-copied but saw same mismatch.
- They confirmed the top-level archive size matched what was provided, but did not verify the provided .sha256 on the air-gapped side prior to extraction.
comments: 2026-01-17 (Dev Patel): Opened per Ion Fabrication escalation. Customer seeing hash mismatch only after transfer/extract. Assigning to Owen for triage. Requested: exact extraction commands, whether bundle was re-zipped, and output of `bundle inspect` if available.

2026-01-17 (Owen Phillips): Asked customer to run on RHEL host:
- `sha256sum -c redwood-private-2026.01.0-offline-bundle.tar.zst.sha256`
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /path/to/redwood-private-2026.01.0-offline-bundle.tar.zst --verify`
Also asked whether they used `unzip -a` / any “text conversion” options on Windows tools.

2026-01-18 (Customer - Ion Fabrication via Support portal): We extracted on Windows using Info-ZIP `unzip -a` because we had issues with scripts having LF line endings in another product. Then we copied the extracted directory tree to Linux. The installer error references `manifests/redwood-private.yaml` and one `values.yaml` file. We did not re-zip.

2026-01-18 (Owen Phillips): Root cause likely `unzip -a` (ASCII/text conversion) rewriting line endings for *.yaml/*.json/*.sh inside the bundle. That will change SHA256 and trigger mismatch against the signed manifest. This aligns with mismatch being deterministic after extraction, not random media corruption.

Remediation path:
1) Re-transfer the original archive without extracting on Windows.
2) Verify archive checksum in the air-gapped environment.
3) Extract using a tool that does not perform line-ending conversion (no `-a` / no "text" mode).

Proposed commands:
- `sha256sum -c redwood-private-2026.01.0-offline-bundle.tar.zst.sha256`
- `mkdir -p /opt/redwood/bundles/2026.01.0 && tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xvf redwood-private-2026.01.0-offline-bundle.tar.zst -C /opt/redwood/bundles/2026.01.0`
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /opt/redwood/bundles/2026.01.0 --verify`

Also advised: do not copy “extracted folder” via Windows file share if there’s any policy tooling that normalizes text files; keep the archive intact until on Linux.

2026-01-19 (Customer - Ion Fabrication): Confirmed. We re-did the process by transporting the `.tar.zst` intact, verified the `.sha256` on the RHEL side, extracted with `tar` (no Windows extraction). Preflight now passes; install succeeded. Maintenance window recovered.

2026-01-19 (Dev Patel): Capturing as docs gap + potential installer messaging improvement. Customer followed old internal guidance that suggested `unzip -a` for cross-platform. Suggest we explicitly warn against any tool/flag that does line-ending conversion. Linking to docs FAQ ticket. Also note: some DLP scanners can rehydrate archives; recommend checksum verify step before extraction.

2026-01-20 (Owen Phillips): Added internal note: If customer must use Windows, recommend 7-Zip extraction with no newline conversion + ensure resulting files are not re-saved by editors. But preferred/lowest-risk is: transport archive intact and extract on target Linux host. Also recommended using `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --verify` prior to install and including output in support bundle.
resolution:
Root cause: customer extracted the offline bundle on Windows with Info-ZIP `unzip -a`, which performs text-mode conversion (line-ending normalization). This modified one or more YAML/manifest files, causing SHA256 mismatches against the signed bundle manifest during installer preflight.

Fix/Workaround applied:
- Customer re-transferred the original archive intact into the air-gapped environment.
- Verified the provided archive checksum (`sha256sum -c …sha256`) on the Linux host.
- Extracted using `tar` on Linux (no text conversion).
- Re-ran preflight; verification succeeded; installation completed.

Follow-ups:
- Update customer-facing docs/FAQ to explicitly warn against `unzip -a` and any newline conversion during extraction/transfer.
- Consider improving installer error message for E_BUNDLE_HASH_MISMATCH to include a hint: “check for text-mode extraction / CRLF conversion; verify archive checksum before extraction.”
